subject: Request: Exception for accelerated multi-year prepay & tier discount
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@veridiansystems.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@veridiansystems.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — multi-year prepay structure and tier exception

Andrew / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, Veridian is excited to commit to a multi-year relationship, but you're asking for an unusual front-loaded ramp and a deeper upfront discount than our standard grid. Specifically you asked for: 70% of year 1 committed up front, then remaining 30% spread across years 2–3, with a 38–40% effective term discount on year‑one pricing.

I've attached the redline and your forecast for reference. Our standard range for a 3‑year prepay is 25–30% at the high-commit tier; anything >35% requires executive approval per our pricing policy.

Can you confirm the commercial objectives you're trying to hit with the larger discount (cashflow vs. unit price), and whether you have any flexibility on the upfront %. That will help me scope the ask to finance/ops when I escalate.

Next steps: I'll loop in Dylan for technical needs and, if we need an exception, escalate to finance/product for a term exception.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: Veridian_MA-Redwood_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 210KB)
From: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@veridiansystems.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@veridiansystems.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@veridiansystems.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year prepay structure and tier exception

Marissa — thanks, appreciate the quick follow.

High level: primary objective is unit economics — we need predictability for budgeting and to present a favorable cost profile to our Board for renewed capital. Secondarily, we want to minimize API egress variability in Q1 next year (we'll be launching 3 new products).

We're fairly firm on the 70% upfront; the 40% term discount stabilizes our COGS plan over 36 months. If Redwood can do 38–40% for the structure below we can sign within two weeks.

Counter-proposal (what we want):
- 3-year term; 70% of Year 1 prepay (billed at contract signature)
- Years 2–3: trued-up annually against usage; committed floors set at 50% of year 1 list usage
- Effective discount on list tokens: 40% year 1, stepping to 32% year 2, 28% year 3 (we want the front-loaded economics).

If this isn't on the table, please outline alternatives and any trade-offs you can make (e.g., higher SLA, optional add-on credits).

—Andrew
Andrew Hayes, Head of Product Partnerships
Veridian Systems
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@veridiansystems.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year prepay structure and tier exception

Andrew — quick note from the product side. The usage profile you described (3 new product launches, spiky Q1 load) is compatible with our burst + prefix caching model, but to meet the latency/throughput guarantees with a large front-loaded commit we should agree on a clear forecast cadence and a headroom policy.

If we sign the 70% up-front, ops will reserve additional dedicated capacity; the main operational ask is a quarterly forecast and a 14-day notice for major traffic shifts. Will Veridian be able to provide that? If so, it reduces our risk significantly and I can support a pricing exception rationale to Finance.

-Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Approval request for non-standard ramp & 38% discount ask (Veridian)

Laura / Karthik —

I need an executive exception for Veridian (DEAL-2026-1175). They are requesting an aggressive front-loaded prepay and a term discount target that exceeds our allowable delegated authority. Key facts:
- Proposed commercial: 3y, 70% Year 1 prepay billed at signature; effective Year1 discount requested: 38–40%
- Business value: large reference customer, multi-product launch in Q1, potential to expand to additional BUs if onboarding is smooth.
- Financials: forecast attached (Prepay-Forecast-VERIDIAN.xlsx). They will provide quarterly forecasts and commit to a 14-day surge notification per Dylan's ask.
- Risk: substantial upfront capacity reservation; we need to make sure cadence and success metrics are enforced (SLA + onboarding milestones).

Requested action: approve an exception to offer up to 38% effective Year1 discount if we get 70% upfront and: signed SOW with onboarding milestones, 12‑month ROI review, and a cancellation clawback for unused prepay in year 1 (pro-rated). If approved, Legal will finalize redline and we can close in 7–10 business days.

Please advise — I can join a quick sync if you want to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Escalation: Approval request for non-standard ramp & 38% discount ask (Veridian)

Team —

I reviewed the ask and the forecast. High-level decision: we can approve an exception but with tightened guardrails. Approve up to 38% effective Year1 discount ONLY under the following conditions: 1) 70% Year1 prepay at signature, 2) legally binding SOW with three onboarding milestones (M1 completion = first 30 days, M2 = production launch, M3 = KPI acceptance at 90 days), 3) 12-month ROI review and revenue clawback for unused Year1 prepay (pro-rata refund schedule capped at 25% of the prepay), 4) strict quarterly forecasting cadence with a 14-day surge notice, and 5) Finance to sign off final payment terms (net 15 ok) and Legal to complete the redline.

Karthik, please prepare the final finance approval memo with the expected cash recognition schedule and break-even sensitivity (best/worst case) so I can sign. Dylan — confirm the operational SLAs and surge procedure language for inclusion in the SOW. Marissa — communicate the approved exception terms to Veridian and push for signature this week.

—Laura
VP, Commercial
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Andrew Hayes <andrew.hayes@veridiansystems.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@veridiansystems.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Approved exception — next steps and doc pack

Andrew — good news: we received executive approval to proceed with an exception. Summary of approved terms (please review):
- 3-year term; 70% of Year1 prepaid at signature
- Effective Year1 discount: 38% (approved cap)
- Governance: legally binding SOW with 3 onboarding milestones, 12-month ROI review, and pro‑rata clawback for unused Year1 prepay (refunds capped at 25% of prepay)
- Operations: quarterly forecasts + 14-day surge notice; Redwood to reserve capacity commensurate with committed usage
- Finance & Legal: net 15 payment terms; Redwood will circulate final redline for signature (attached).

Next steps: I'll send the final redline to your Legal/Procurement and schedule a 30‑minute closure call for Wed morning. If you can confirm acceptance of the governance points above, we'll get Legal/Finance to push the DocuSign.

Thanks — excited to get Veridian live.

Best,
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Veridian_MA-Redwood_v3_redline.pdf (updated)
